note: item codes ARE the .sav column names (data/onah_2021_covid_literacy.py keeps them verbatim; no rename, no positional step). Mapping tie: SPSS-DATA-COVID-19.sav variable labels, 10/10 (e.g. WHO_website='WHO website', From_church_or_mosque='from church or mosque'). Wording: the deposit's Questionnaire--ASSESSMEnt.pdf, Section 2 Cluster 1 table, transcribed verbatim incl. its casing ('from church or mosque'); only difference from the .sav labels is the social-media example list, PDF 'Social media (facebook, twitter, whatsapp etc.)' vs label 'Social media (facebook, twitter, etc)' -- PDF wording shipped. Options: PDF column headers 'Agree'/'Disagree'; .sav value labels 1='agree',2='disagree'; processing script ships agree->1, disagree->0, so option_text Agree=1, Disagree=0 -- confirmed by route 9 (all 20 item x level counts match). Instrument field = questionnaire title plus the cluster heading. Administered in English (Nigeria, online survey). Rights: study's own questionnaire in a CC BY 4.0 Mendeley deposit; no instrument-level restriction exists or was found. The Google Form linked from the deposit (docs.google.com/forms/d/1lexlFeQ4da6C_JCl0yWUHtoxXOe2dnP0aYU8UJdECBY) was fetched 2026-09-25 and has been edited since collection: its Cluster 1 block is now a single dropdown headed 'which of these following sources do you consult for COVID-19 related health information?' with one option ('from church or mosque'), its gender field is labelled 'Male ' with a lone 'female' option, and it carries an unrelated 'Senior Seminar Presentation' block. That stem may be what respondents read, but the form no longer reflects the administered instrument, so it was NOT shipped as instructions; instructions are blank because the deposited questionnaire PDF gives none for Cluster 1.

source_ref: Onah U, Momohjimoh A, Okonkwo E (2021) 'Health information literacy of Nigerians on the preventive measures of COVID-19: A cross sectional survey data', Mendeley Data doi:10.17632/cf3s3v8wb3, CC BY 4.0 (public-api data_licence). Files: Questionnaire--ASSESSMEnt.pdf (file 81d225e6-c0a9-470e-9172-1d55a36f8f91, sha256 prefix f85b93af8d567987), Cluster 2 'COVID 19 Health Related Information Literacy Assessment Scale', items 1-25 with lettered alternatives; SPSS-DATA-COVID-19.sav (file 61f7a311-78ae-468f-9b84-a965b23a901b, sha256 prefix 524a1278e2585f8b), variable labels and value labels of COVID_1..COVID_25; processing script data/onah_2021_covid_literacy.py.
note: mapping_basis=data_labels: the IRW item code is the .sav column name unchanged (the script melts COVID_1..COVID_25 without renaming), and each column's SPSS variable label reproduces questionnaire item n's stem, 25/25 (differences only: the label drops a trailing '?' on item 2, the '……'/'…' on items 3 and 7, the final '.' on item 22, and has a double space in item 25). text_source=study_materials: item_text is the questionnaire PDF's stem followed by its lettered alternatives on one line ('a. ... b. ...'); the '( )' tick boxes were dropped and line wraps joined, otherwise verbatim incl. source typos ('alcoholic be based', 'is recommended is a preventive measure', 'Keeping 1 meters'). The alternatives are folded into item_text because the table stores only a correct/incorrect score, so there is no resp level to attach them to. instructions = the Cluster 2 instruction sentence verbatim minus its 'Instruction:' label (it mentions 4 marks per correct answer; IRW scores 1/0). option_text 'correct'/'incorrect' = the .sav's own value labels (lowercase as written; COVID_11 misspells level 1 'icorrect'). The raw polarity is not constant: COVID_11, 12, 15, 21, 22, 23 label 2='correct', the other 19 label 1='correct'; the processing script recodes per item from the value labels to resp 1=correct, 0=incorrect. Route 9 confirms: live count of resp==1 equals the .sav count of the item's 'correct' code for 25/25 items, and 0/6 flipped items match a naive 1->1 recode. correct_response left blank: neither the questionnaire nor the deposit states which alternative was keyed correct; not derived. English administration (online Google Form, Nigeria), so no language/_translated columns. Rights: the authors' own questionnaire deposited under CC BY 4.0; not a third-party instrument; no restriction located.
public_note: Respondents chose among the lettered alternatives shown in item_text, but the data record only whether the answer was scored correct (resp 1) or incorrect (0); the source does not publish which alternative was keyed correct.

note: Clean gate pass (batch_453), 196 rows = 28 items x 7 levels; validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (28/28 items, resp 1-7). CODE DERIVATION: positional -- the script assigns ams01..ams28 in column order to the 28 xlsx columns starting 'NEDEN OKULA', id = row index. The headers carry each item's full Turkish wording in brackets, so mapping_basis=data_labels, and the positional step was checked rather than exempted: header diff 28/28, and re-deriving from the raw xlsx reproduces the live table 11536/11536 cells (no two source columns identical; min 141 respondents differ between any pair). TEXT: item_text = the bracketed header text verbatim, including its leading '... ' (the form's grid rows continue the stem 'NEDEN OKULA GIDIYORSUNUZ? Cunku ...', which is the grid title and ships once in instructions). 28/28 match Unal-Karaguven (2012) Ek.1 items 1-28 after normalising ellipses/dot leaders/quotes, so the study used that published Turkish form, whose numbering is the canonical AMS-C 28 order. ANCHORS: the deposit carries none (values stored as integers 1-7). option_text for 1/4/7 is taken from Ek.1 (Hic uyusmuyor / Orta derecede Uyusuyor / Tam olarak Uyusuyor), whose labels sit over 1, 4 and 7; 'Biraz uyusuyor' and 'Oldukca Uyusuyor' are printed between 2-3 and 5-6, so 2, 3, 5, 6 ship blank rather than guessing a point. Not confirmed that the study's Google Form showed these labels. ENGLISH (_translated): items and anchors are Vallerand's own AMS-C 28 English (emec_en.pdf) for the same numbered items -- a parallel version, not a translation of the Turkish string; the instructions' 'Because ...' is IRW's rendering of 'Cunku ...' appended to Vallerand's 'WHY DO YOU GO TO COLLEGE ?'. Hence translation_source=mixed. RIGHTS: both originators grant attribution-only use. Vallerand emec_en.pdf: 'Note: To use this scale you require only to mention the complete reference data.' Unal-Karaguven 2012 Ek.1: 'Not: Olcegi kullanmak icin referanslari belirtmek yeterli olacaktir.' (To use the scale, citing the references is sufficient.) Neither reserves a fee, permission, NC, ND or redistribution right. The AMS is Vallerand's (LRCS/UQAM), not in the CSDT library register row (matches reaudit/triage_results.csv row 7 lead). PsycTESTS records t71717-000 / t54064-000 were unreadable (Incapsula block); the adapter's own printed grant is the originator statement. No register row written (rounds may not write ship rows).
